name: CONCATENATE
description: CONCATENATE joins two or more text items into one text string. It is the legacy join function; CONCAT and TEXTJOIN are newer and more flexible.

parameters.name: text1
parameters.description: The first text item or cell reference to join.

parameters.name: text2
parameters.description: Additional text items or cell references to join (optional, up to 255 arguments).

basicExample.explanation: The three text items are concatenated in order into a single string.

advancedExamples.title: Build a full name from cells
advancedExamples.explanation: Cell references and literal text are joined seamlessly.

advancedExamples.title: Prefer TEXTJOIN for ranges
advancedExamples.scenario: Join A1:A3 without listing each cell
advancedExamples.result: Items joined by a comma and space
advancedExamples.explanation: TEXTJOIN accepts a range and delimiter directly, which CONCATENATE cannot do in one argument.

howItWorks: CONCATENATE accepts up to 255 text arguments and appends them in the order given, returning one combined text string. It does not add any separator on its own.

howToSteps.name: List the items
howToSteps.text: Decide which texts or cells to join.

howToSteps.name: Add separators
howToSteps.text: Include literal separators like " " as their own arguments.

limitations: Cannot accept a range as a single argument; each cell must be listed separately.
Adds no delimiter automatically, so separators must be supplied manually.
Superseded by CONCAT (ranges) and TEXTJOIN (delimiters, ignore empties) in newer Excel.

commonErrors.cause: Referencing a range directly, e.g. =CONCATENATE(A1:A3), in versions that disallow it.
commonErrors.fix: List cells individually or use CONCAT/TEXTJOIN for ranges.

googleSheetsEquivalent.description: CONCATENATE works the same in Google Sheets, but the CONCAT and TEXTJOIN successors are also available and recommended for ranges.
googleSheetsEquivalent.notes: Identical legacy behavior; prefer TEXTJOIN for ranges.

faq.question: Should I use CONCATENATE or TEXTJOIN?
faq.answer: Use TEXTJOIN when joining a range or adding a delimiter; CONCATENATE is legacy.

faq.question: Can CONCATENATE join a range?
faq.answer: Not as a single argument; you must list each cell, or use CONCAT/TEXTJOIN.

faq.question: What is the 255 limit?
faq.answer: CONCATENATE accepts up to 255 individual text arguments.
